Biz, uzay bilimleri, teknoloji ve sağlık alanlarına ilgi duyan, yenilikçi çözümler üretmeyi hedefleyen bir ekibiz. Projemiz, uzay görevlerindeki astronotların kalp atış hızı, vücut sıcaklığı ve oksijen seviyeleri gibi sağlık verilerini takip edebilen bir yazılım geliştirmektir.

Ekibimize katılanlarla fikir alışverişi yaparak bilimsel ve teknolojik çözümler geliştirmeyi amaçlıyoruz.

details:
ASTRA-GUARD – Project Details

ASTRA-GUARD is an intelligent hazard detection and early warning system designed to improve astronaut safety in space environments, particularly aboard the International Space Station (ISS) and in future human habitats on the Moon and Mars.

How Does It Work?

The system combines two different hazard detection mechanisms into a single microcontroller-based platform.

The first mechanism uses a distance sensor to detect objects approaching within approximately 30 cm. In microgravity environments, objects can move freely and create unexpected collision risks for astronauts. When an object enters the defined detection range, the system triggers an audible and/or visual warning, helping astronauts become aware of potential hazards.

The second mechanism uses a gas sensor to monitor the surrounding environment for specific harmful gases. If the detected gas level reaches a predefined threshold, the system generates an alert to warn astronauts about a potential gas-related danger.

A microcontroller processes data from both sensors, evaluates the detected conditions, and displays system information on an LCD screen. This allows both physical and chemical hazards to be monitored through a single integrated prototype.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA-GUARD aims to provide early detection of potential dangers before they become serious threats. Its main benefits include:

  • Detecting approaching objects and reducing potential collision risks.
  • Identifying specific harmful gases and warning astronauts about possible leaks.
  • Monitoring two different categories of hazards simultaneously.
  • Providing real-time information through an LCD display.
  • Supporting astronaut awareness and faster responses to dangerous situations.

The intended impact is to contribute to safer and more sustainable human activities in space. In the long term, the system could be further developed for use in space stations and human habitats on the Moon and Mars.

Tools, Hardware, and Technologies

The prototype was developed using a microcontroller-based electronic system. Its main components include:

  • A microcontroller for processing sensor data and controlling the system.
  • A distance sensor for detecting approaching objects.
  • A gas sensor for detecting specific harmful gases.
  • An LCD screen for displaying system information.
  • Electronic connection components and circuit wiring.
  • An audible and/or visual warning mechanism.

The microcontroller is programmed to receive sensor data, evaluate predefined detection thresholds, and activate the appropriate warning mechanisms. The project uses embedded programming and electronic circuit integration to ensure that all components work together.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of ASTRA-GUARD lies in combining two different safety functions within a single integrated system. Instead of monitoring physical collision risks and chemical hazards separately, our project brings both functions together under one control mechanism.

This integrated approach offers a practical, expandable, and potentially low-cost safety solution. Its modular structure also makes it possible to add new sensors and functions in future versions.

Factors Considered by the Team

During the development process, our team considered astronaut safety, early hazard detection, system response time, sensor accuracy, ease of use, portability, cost, and expandability.

We also considered the special conditions of space environments, particularly microgravity and the risks associated with confined living spaces. We recognize that the current prototype must undergo additional testing under simulated space conditions before it can be considered suitable for actual space missions.

ASTRA-GUARD represents an initial step toward developing smarter and more integrated safety technologies for the future of human exploration beyond Earth. AI
